newsitem.title: GREECE: Four more Greek brokers barred from trade.
newsitem.headline: Four more Greek brokers barred from trade.

text.p: Four more Athens brokers were barred from trading on the bourse for one day on Thursday as the turmoil caused by the Delta Securities settlement scandal showed no sign of abating.

A number of brokerages have been banned from trading for a day recently after failing to settle trades within 48 hours, a rule which officials have been strictly imposing since the Delta scandal rocked the bourse this month.
Alpha Credit Bank subsidiary Alpha Brokerage, Beta Securities, Portalakis Brokerage and Komninos Brokerage were suspended from trading on Thursday.

"We have a network of 200 branches so you can imagine that in cities outside Athens and with (today's) the post on strike it is practically impossible to be sure the 48-hour deadline will be met. A client may be a bit late in bringing shares," Dimitris Verriopoulos at Alpha Brokerage said.
Alpha Brokerage, one of the largest in terms of market share delivered shares worth 21 million drachmas to the clearing house on Thursday morning instead of the 1430 hours deadline on Wednesday.

Delta tried to settle deals with 2.6 billion drachmas in bad cheques, apparently hoping a clearing backlog would provide the time to find sufficient funds. Three Delta officials have been charged with fraud.

The insistence on the tight 48-hour deadline coupled with suspensions of large and small brokerages has sent daily volume down to around the year's lows of two billion drachmas, brokers said. They said the bourse's reputation was being damaged.

Alpha, for instance, had a problem with a foreign client who made an error on an order to his custodians. By the time the chain from global custodian, to local custodian, to broker fixed the error, it was too late to meet the deadline.

"With this settlement rule there will always be problems," said Verriopoulos. "But the clearing house only applies the rule on one side. When it comes to deliver to brokers they are late to deliver shares to us by four or five days."
Officials at Beta Securities were concerned the stock market was being damaged by the new obsession with rigidly applying the settlement rule.

"We had a buy and sell order on the same day. The clearing house delivered registered shares due us at 14:30 and told us we should have delivered our part at 14:00. So we were suspended," said broker Evangelos Haratsis at Beta.
He alleged that authorities were being unfair and selective when suspending exchange members from trade.
"Based on the rule 17 brokers should have been suspended on Thursday and they picked just four," he told Reuters.

Similar complaints were voiced on Wednesday by Hermes Brokerage, which said 31 brokers should have been suspended for non-compliance, including two state bank subsidiaries. But only three were expelled.
Brokers are also concerned that the practical details of the problem are not understood by the investment public with the end result damaging the bourse's overall reputation.
"The stock market as an institution should not allow a relaxed regulatory environment but should also avoid extremes and exaggeration," said broker Zacharias Portalakis.
"Without share dematerialisation (electronic book entry instead of physical paper), what do you do when you have a client in the countryside and must meet a 48-hour settlement deadline?" he asked.
